plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Fragrant, blossom-laden branches burst into flower on bare winter twigs. The blooms are delicate, five-petaled and spicy-sweet, and they often open while cold still lingers. Ume groves in Japan are a much-loved sign that spring is near.
plants.location: Japan, southern China, Taiwan and Korea
plants.funFact: The fruits of this tree are pickled in salt to make umeboshi, the tangy preserved plums that are a staple of Japanese cuisine.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding white bells hang from slender stems just above the cold ground, often pushing up through frost or even snow. Drifts of snowdrops carpet woodlands, parks and churchyards and mark the first stirrings of spring.
plants.location: Woodlands, parks and gardens across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrop flowers are made of six white segments called tepals rather than true petals. Their flowering is now often recorded earlier than it once was, with some blooms appearing as early as December.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: Bare, sturdy stalks shoot up from dry ground at the end of summer, each topped with a cluster of fragrant, trumpet-shaped flowers in shades of pink. The leaves only appear after the show is over, which gives the blooms a dramatic, leafless stage.
plants.funFact: This bulb flowers before its leaves emerge, a habit called hysteranthy. That habit is why it is nicknamed the naked lady.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs are covered in rose-like blooms that brighten shady gardens in the last weeks of winter. Many varieties are available, with flowers ranging from simple cups to fully layered, formal forms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to spring, with many varieties peaking in late winter to early spring
plants.location: Mild-climate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere (USDA zones 7–9), native to East Asia
plants.funFact: By staggering early, mid and late-blooming varieties, gardeners can enjoy camellia flowers from November right through to April or May.
